Location Our Technical Product Owner - DoiT Cloud Intelligence - Core Services will be an integral part of our global Product team. This role is based remotely in the East Coast US, the UK, Ireland, Estonia, the Netherlands, Sweden and Israel.

Who We Are DoiT is a global technology company that works with cloud-driven organizations to leverage the cloud to drive business growth and innovation. We combine data, technology, and human expertise to ensure our customers operate in a well-architected and scalable state - from planning to production.

Delivering DoiT Cloud Intelligence, the only solution that integrates advanced technology with human intelligence, we help our customers solve complex multi-cloud problems and drive efficiency. With decades of multi-cloud experience, we have specializations in Kubernetes, GenAI, CloudOps, and more.

An award-winning strategic partner of AWS, Google Cloud, and Microsoft Azure, we work alongside more than 4,000 customers worldwide.

The Opportunity We’re hiring a Technical Product Owner to drive rapid delivery and iteration for the Core Services team of DoiT Cloud Intelligence, our platform that helps DevOps, Cloud Infrastructure, and FinOps teams manage public cloud environments effectively and efficiently.

Core Services builds and operates foundational platform capabilities used across DoiT’s products and engineering teams. Its responsibilities include identity and access management, authentication and authorization, customer and tenant services, shared APIs, platform integrations, and other cross-cutting capabilities.

This role is designed for someone with a technical product mindset who is comfortable working deep within platform architecture, distributed systems, APIs, cloud infrastructure, and internal engineering workflows.

You will help turn broad platform needs into clear technical product direction, sequenced investments, and reliably delivered capabilities. You will report to a VP of Product and work as an embedded member of the Core Services Engineering team.

You will collaborate closely with engineering leadership, architects, security, product teams, and internal platform consumers to determine what the team should build next and why. Role clarity: VP of Product vs. Technical Product Owner VP of Product (what they own)
Sets the overall vision, strategy, positioning, and long-range roadmap for the platform area.
Makes the highest-level prioritization calls across multiple components and investment themes.
Aligns stakeholders across the company (executive leadership, GTM, partners) on direction and tradeoffs.
Defines success at the portfolio/area level and ensures the area’s outcomes ladder up to company goals.
Technical Product Owner (what you own)
Owns delivery, iteration, and learning velocity for the Core Services.
Turns VP-level direction into clear problems to solve, a prioritized backlog, and incrementally shippable scope.
Runs the feedback loop: discover → define → build → release → measure → iterate, repeatedly.
Works within the Engineering teams to ensure they are always building the highest-value next increment with clarity, quality
Review technical designs, reason about tradeoffs and constraints, and understand their impact on delivery timelines and system behavior, without being the primary implementer
Leverages deep, hands-on DevOps experience and public cloud understanding to ensure that solution implementations are done correctly
This distinction matters: the VP creates the “why” and “where”; the Product Owner ensures the “what next” is always sharp, validated, and shipping. Responsibilities Fast iteration and backlog leadership
Translate the VP’s strategy into a sequenced backlog of problems, user stories, and acceptance criteria that the Engineering team can deliver continuously.
Keep work “thin-sliced” so the team can ship frequently, learn quickly, and reduce risk through iteration.
Maintain a disciplined cadence of backlog refinement, sprint readiness, and scope negotiation to keep delivery predictable without slowing innovation.
Deep user and workflow understanding
Leverage your hands-on DevOps experience and expertise in the real-world workflows of the professionals you’re building for - especially cloud operators and practitioners.
Use firsthand domain knowledge and ongoing customer conversations to identify friction, gaps, and opportunities for differentiation.
Prioritize enhancements that materially improve outcomes: speed, reliability, clarity, safety, governance, cost impact, or operational simplicity.
Customer validation and external communication
Often speak with customers (aiming for 3-5 calls a week) and cross-functional DoiT stakeholders regularly to test ideas, validate assumptions, and pressure-test tradeoffs.
Communicate clearly and confidently: share concepts early, take feedback openly, synthesize input into decisions, and explain “why” in a way that builds trust.
Rely on your hands-on, DevOps experience to go deep with stakeholders (internal/external) into the technical details of the problem, our solution, and the contexts and environments in which both of these exist.
Support beta/design-partner motions where appropriate by shaping hypotheses, success criteria, and rollout plans.
Engineering-embedded technical product ownership
Operate as a core member of the Core Services’ Engineering team - present in daily collaboration, crisp in decision-making, and pragmatic about constraints.
Partner with Engineering leads on sequencing, technical tradeoffs, and delivery planning - ensuring product intent survives implementation realities.
Ensure Core Services are cohesive across UX, APIs, data, and operational behavior - and that it meets a high bar for reliability and customer trust.
Quality, outcomes, and measurement
Define what “success” means for Core Services with clear metrics (adoption, activation, workflow completion, time-to-value, retention, reliability signals, customer-reported impact).
Instrument learning: make sure releases are measurable and that insights reliably flow back into prioritization.
Own release readiness for Core Services: documentation, enablement inputs, and clear communication of what’s new and why it matters.
Safety, governance, and trust by design
Ensure product requirements account for real-world cloud environments: IAM boundaries, auditability, guardrails, and safe defaults.
Partner with security, support, and customer teams to anticipate edge cases and ensure Core Services earns trust over time.

7–10 years of hands-on experience as a Platform Engineer, DevOps Engineer, SRE, Cloud Engineer, Solutions Architect, or a similar roles working with or building products for public cloud infrastructure (AWS, GCP, and/or Azure).
A strong product sense for turning messy problems into clear scope and shipped value - without waiting for perfect information.
Systems thinking: Ability to reason about complex distributed systems, architectural tradeoffs, and long-term platform evolution.
Prioritization: Demonstrated ability to balance customer needs, engineering constraints, and platform investments when making prioritization decisions.

Imagine the what. Build the how.

Your opportunity
As a Product Manager for ShelfView Capture , you will own the strategy and roadmap for how ShelfView acquires shelf data — a cornerstone of ShelfView's hybrid data capture . You'll work at the intersection of UX, mobile engineering, and computer vision to make capture fast, simple, and reliable, and to ensure the right shelf data is collected at the right quality, coverage, and cost.
ShelfView turns images and video from mobile devices, fixed cameras, and autonomous robots into a digital twin of the store, generating insights that remove tedious tasks for retail workers. Your mission is to make the capture experience best-in-class for accuracy, cost, and speed.

Partner with customers and field teams to understand capture environments and translate needs into requirements.
Build and drive the ShelfView capture roadmap toward high throughput, coverage, and quality at the right cost.
Define and deliver a better capture experience (e.g., improved video capture, AR guidance, faster and more reliable first-time-right capture).
Own how capture work is tasked and scheduled — which stores and aisles are captured, how often, and by whom.
Own store onboarding and modeling — getting stores ready (mapping, planograms, catalogs) and keeping them current as stores change.
Define capture quality, product metrics, and telemetry , and run experiments to inform iterative development.
Work closely with design, mobile engineering, and CV teams to evaluate new technologies that improve capture success
Drive non-mobile, hybrid capture (fixed camera, robot and emerging technologies).
Coordinate feature launches with product marketing and sales operations; act as the capture point of contact on pilots and early customer rollouts.

Degree in Engineering or a related field.
6+ years of product management experience in a "Deep Tech" or mobile SaaS company, or equivalent product leadership experience in a startup.
Experience with mobile apps, AR use-cases, or on-device ML is beneficial.
Strong problem-solving and analytical skills to identify user needs; comfortable working hands-on with data/telemetry.
Open-minded, sociable, and driven personality.
Excellent English communication skills, both written and oral.
Eligible to work in Switzerland.
Ability to visit customers in Europe and North America on occasion.
You will either be living within a commutable distance of our Zurich office.

s.h: Some key info for you about Liberis
s.t:
🌱 We were founded in 2007

💰 We have provided over $3bn of funding to small businesses so far

🚀 We have been named in CNBC & Statista Top 150 UK Fintechs for 2025

🌍 We're a global team, with a dynamic presence in 6 key locations around the world

💪 We’re proud to be an accredited Real Living Wage employer, ensuring everyone is paid fairly for the great work they do!

Liberis is in the middle of a meaningful shift. We started as a single-product business and are quickly becoming a truly multi-product embedded finance company, with different funding structures, revenue models and customer relationships sitting alongside each other in the same portfolio. That complexity creates real demand for better data, better insight and clearer thinking about how all of it fits together - with this role sitting at the centre of that challange!

As our Senior Data Product Manager, you’ll sit right at the intersection of product, analytics, engineering and senior leadership, helping define the data products that power smarter decisions across Liberis.

You’ll have real ownership over roadmap, prioritisation and ways of working, and your work will directly influence how teams access, understand and use data day to day. This role is a high-impact opportunity for someone who wants to shape how a business uses data at scale!

You’ll be joining a team with a broad remit and a genuine mandate to improve the data experience across the company, so there’s a lot of scope to make the role your own and shape the future of the domain.

You will own the data and insights product for Liberis, building the foundations that let our commercial, credit and operations teams actually understand the business they're running.

That means, thinking carefully about the entities in our data model, how products and customers relate to each other, how those relationships surface in reporting and analysis - and how it eventually all comes out in great dashboards, tools and self-serve capabilities.

This is about shipping products which are genuinely useful, not just technically correct.

Our Engineering Team is going through an AI-first transformation, rethinking how teams are structured and how they ship. Data, insights and analytics are a crucial part of that journey and you will be a key player in leading, innovating and rapidly improving our posture and capabilities at the intersection of data and AI.

If you like solving genuinely hard problems, bringing clarity to complex environments and building products that have visible business impact - this is the role for you!

Your primary job is to help Liberis's commercial decision makers understand the small businesses we serve and how they consider, use and perform across our product range. Doing this well requires a clear conceptual model of the business and a willingness to engage with stakeholders across the business, as well as taste and customer empathy in developing a great insights product including dashboards, insight tools and self-serve capabilities.

You will own the roadmap for our internal data & insight products. Working with stakeholders across commercial, credit, finance and operations, you will define what good looks like and then work with your team to build it. You will run prioritisation, manage the backlog and make decisions about where effort goes.

You will also spend a meaningful amount of time in the detail, reviewing data models and dashboards, asking hard questions about definitions, and making sure what we ship is accurate and trusted.

You will partner closely with the engineering side of your team on how data is modelled and structured in BigQuery and DBT, and with analysts on how it gets presented in Looker. You don't need to write production code, but you need enough technical understanding to be a genuine partner in those conversations. You will also be responsible for continuing to expand our partner-facing reporting, whereby partners gain visibility into their portfolio.

This role requires someone who can think clearly about complex data structures and translate that thinking into products that non-technical people actually find useful. The ideal person has strong conceptual thinking skills, great product instincts and enough technical depth to earn the trust of the engineers and analysts they work with.

· Proven experience in a senior data product or analytics product role in a business with real complexity

· A track record of helping commercial teams make better decisions through better data, not just shipping dashboards

· Strong ability to think about entities, taxonomies and relationships in data

· Hands-on experience with Looker and LookML and familiarity with best practices and scalable approaches to these systems

· Working knowledge of SQL, DBT and BigQuery, enough to engage seriously with how data is modelled and what's feasible, and to express your thinking in code-speak where needed

· Experience working with a multi skilled team of analysts and data engineers

· Clear, confident communication with senior commercial stakeholders

Next steps If this opportunity feels like the right fit for your next career move, we’d love to hear from you!

Even if you don’t meet every requirement, don’t hesitate to apply or reach out to Chess (Internal Recruiter) on

Our hybrid approach

Working together in person helps us move faster, collaborate better, and build a great Liberis culture. Our hybrid working policy requires team members to be in the office at least 3 days a week, but ideally 4 days. At Liberis, we embrace flexibility as a core part of our culture, while also valuing the importance of the time our teams spend together in the office.

About ScholarshipOwl
ScholarshipOwl is the largest scholarship marketplace in the U.S., connecting over 14 million Gen Z students with private scholarships — and the brands that power them. Our mission is to make education financing more accessible and engaging, while giving brands a way to connect with the next generation.
We’re powered by AI technology that simplifies scholarship discovery, streamlines the application process, and delivers measurable results for both students and partners. Whether it’s helping students secure funding or enabling brands to run impactful campaigns, we’re reshaping how education is funded — and discovered.

We’re looking for a Growth Product Manager to take full ownership of the conversion engine at ScholarshipOwl, from the first visitor touchpoint through to a paid subscription. This is a high-impact, high-velocity role for someone who lives in the data, thrives on experimentation, and values action over perfection.
You will be the architect of our growth. You’ll spend your days identifying leaks in the funnel, hypothesizing solutions, and working alongside a dedicated pod of engineers and designers to ship experiments that move the needle on revenue and retention. If you are a "full-stack" growth thinker who can move from a Mixpanel cohort analysis to a detailed technical spec this is the role for you.

Own the Conversion Engine: Take end-to-end responsibility for the user journey, optimizing every step from landing page registration to paywall conversion and subscription retention.
Drive the Experiment Roadmap: Build, prioritize, and maintain a high-tempo experimentation backlog. You will use frameworks (like ICE or RICE) to ensure we are always working on the highest-leverage growth bets.
Analyze & Diagnose: Monitor funnel and retention metrics daily in Mixpanel. You’ll identify exactly where users are dropping off and perform deep-dive discovery to understand the why .
Ship with Velocity: Write precise product specs and acceptance criteria that allow engineering and design to execute independently. We prioritize shipping "good enough" tests today to get data, rather than waiting for "perfect" features next month.
Optimize Revenue Levers: Design and run pricing, paywall, and offer optimization tests. You’ll also evaluate new growth levers like organic loops, landing page personalization, and winback programs.
Collaborate Cross-Functionally: Lead a dedicated pod of engineers and designers, maintaining strong working relationships with our dashboard and B2B teams to drive unified sprint priorities.
Continuous Discovery: Conduct meaningful customer discovery interviews with our Gen-Z audience to uncover behavioral insights that data alone can’t show.

4+ years of Product Management experience , specifically in a **Growth-**focused role.
Experimentation Mastery: Proven track record of designing, running, and analyzing A/B tests that resulted in measurable improvements to business KPIs (CVR, ARPU, Churn).
Data Fluency: You are a power user of product analytics tools (Mixpanel, Amplitude, or similar). You don't wait for a data analyst; you find the answers yourself.
SaaS/Subscription Expertise: You understand the nuances of subscription models—trial-to-paid transitions, renewal cycles, and friction-point reduction.
Technical Precision: Ability to write clear, "dev-ready" product specs and acceptance criteria. You understand technical trade-offs and how to scope an MVP.
Mentoring & Leadership: A mentoring and knowledge-sharing mindset with a desire to level up the broader team on growth methodologies and experimentation rigor.
Gen-Z Empathy: You have an intuition for (or experience with) B2C products targeting younger audiences and understand their unique digital behaviors.
Growth Mindset: You are comfortable with ambiguity, fast-moving environments, and the fact that 70% of experiments might fail—as long as we learn from them.

Experience with payment platforms (Stripe, Braintree) or Figma/prototyping tools.
Knowledge of lifecycle/email marketing , SEO , and paid acquisition channels.
Growth-focused certifications (e.g., Reforge).
Background in EdTech or student-facing products.

The Lead Technical Product Owner serves as the bridge between business strategy, product vision, architecture, and engineering execution. The ideal candidate possesses a strong combination of product ownership, solution architecture, enterprise integration, and software engineering expertise.

This individual will partner closely with business stakeholders, architects, engineering teams, and operations partners to deliver reliable, scalable, and secure technology solutions while continuously improving delivery efficiency through automation and AI adoption. Translate business objectives into technical capabilities, features, epics, and user stories.
Drive backlog refinement, PI planning, release planning, and sprint execution activities.
Partner with Product Managers, business stakeholders, architects, QA, and engineering teams to ensure successful delivery.
Prioritize features, enhancements, technical debt, and operational improvements based on business value and risk.
Establish clear product goals, success metrics, and delivery milestones.

Coordinate cross-functional efforts to deliver seamless customer and business experiences.
Production Stability & Operational Excellence

Semarchy has grown into an industry leader in the data management space. We're searching for a Product Manager to help expand the Semarchy Data Platform (SDP) and support our development teams. As a Product Manager, you are one of our core creative talents.

Reporting to the Head of Product Management and working closely with engineering, design, and the field, you will turn customer problems and market evidence into product capabilities that customers value — and pay for. Your goal will be to increase the adoption and market fit of the Semarchy Data Platform.

You will own your product scope end-to-end: discovering what customers actually need, framing the problems worth solving, prioritizing ruthlessly, shaping the roadmap, and partnering across teams to bring capabilities to market successfully.

Your early focus is likely to involve Semarchy 's AI-oriented capabilities — such as agentic access to governed Data Products and AI-assisted stewardship — so experience or genuine enthusiasm in this area is a real advantage.

As with any growing product organization, scope and responsibilities will be shaped together and are expected to evolve over time. We are therefore looking for someone adaptable and curious, who thrives when the problem space is still taking shape. Responsibilities
Discovery & customer research: Run structured problem discovery — investigate problem spaces, validate pain intensity and business impact, map current alternatives, and confirm willingness to change. Engage continuously with customers and partners, including active participation in design partner programs.
Focus on customer value: Anchor every decision in customer outcomes rather than mechanisms. Be able to articulate the customer, the problem, and why it matters — and bring that evidence into product decisions.
Roadmapping & prioritization: Own and maintain the roadmap for your area with regular reviews, clear milestones, and transparent change rationale. Prioritize using evidence rather than assumption, make deliberate trade-offs, and contribute to a monthly-updated, prioritized roadmap that reflects what the market actually needs.
Delivery: Partner closely with engineering and design through the full product delivery lifecycle, from discovery to release. Produce specifications and UI concepts, and refine and organize the product backlog — shaping the end-to-end experience, not just features.
Commercialization & field enablement: Play a key role in the commercialization process, coordinating the activities within your scope — such as internal training, previews, enablement, and messaging — so releases reach customers fully field-ready. Contribute captivating documentation and customer-facing assets (blogs, whitepapers, solution briefs) that help the field and marketing communicate value, and participate in commercialization retrospectives.
AI-oriented capabilities (initial focus): Shape how customers connect their enterprise AI ecosystem to governed, trusted data (e.g., agentic / MCP-based access). Explore and validate AI-assisted stewardship and governed AI participation, and help translate fast-moving AI research and prototypes into shippable, differentiated value.
Evangelism: Champion Semarchy products to internal and external audiences — talking to customers, partners, industry analysts, and field personnel — and feed their input back into product strategy and prioritization.

Proven experience as a product manager or product owner in the B2B, SaaS, or technology space, with a solid portfolio.
Demonstrated strength in customer discovery and research — you have talked to many customers and turned what you heard into product decisions.
A clear bias toward value and outcomes — comfortable challenging requests and reframing them around the underlying problem.
Strong prioritization and roadmapping discipline, with the ability to communicate decisions and trade-offs to technical and non-technical stakeholders.
Solid experience in product ownership, including backlog management, requirements gathering, and specification production.
Technical ability to interact with expert developers on topics such as software architecture, databases, APIs, and user interfaces.
Proven ability to quickly learn and understand market topics and technical concepts.
Working knowledge of modern AI architectures and integration patterns (e.g., LLMs, RAG, MCP, vector databases, agents, and AI APIs), with the ability to translate emerging capabilities into enterprise product strategy and requirements.
Comfort operating with evolving scope and ambiguity — you thrive when the problem space is still taking shape.
Fluent in English and French; communication skills to collaborate, present, and evangelize the Semarchy vision and products.
Ability to handle multiple priorities simultaneously while remaining flexible and consistently hitting deadlines.

Full-Time
New York, Chicago or Charlotte

About Oula
Oula Health is a venture-backed, midwifery-led maternity and GYN care company building the next generation of women's healthcare. We partner exclusively with major health systems — including Mount Sinai, Stamford Health, and Novant Health — to embed our collaborative OB-GYN and midwifery model directly inside their networks. We're a team of ~100 people at Series B stage, with 4 clinics today and three more opening in 2026.

At Oula, our product doesn't sit alongside our EHR — it integrates directly into it. Every product and engineering decision has downstream consequences for how our EHRs are configured, and every EHR configuration decision shapes what's possible on the product side. Someone has to hold both at once.
We're looking for a technically-minded Product Manager to own and evolve our core technology stack — including our EHR, patient portal, and care management platform. This role sits at the intersection of product, operations, and health system integration, serving as the internal and external subject matter expert on our EMR and the primary lead for health system EHR integrations.
You'll manage the day-to-day health of our tech stack, partnering closely with both internal teams and external health system stakeholders to ensure our systems run smoothly and our integrations deliver.

You can sit with a midwife and understand why a clinical template matters, then turn around and write a bug ticket that engineering can actually action, then build the SOP so the next market launch doesn't require you to be in the room. When things are ambiguous (and they often are), you'll lean in rather than wait for clarity.
What You'll Own
EHR Configuration & Clinical Systems
Own day-to-day management of our core tech stack: the EHR, patient portal, and care management platform
Own Athena and Epic configuration end to end: clinical templates, order sets, lab configurations, payer connectivity, and access management for clinical and ops staff
Lead EHR integration efforts as the internal and external subject matter expert — FHIR/HL7 data exchange, health system IT coordination and committed go-live timelines
Own and accelerate Epic integration timelines as we onboard additional health system partners
Maintain configuration integrity as new markets launch and care model workflows evolve
Partner with our IT team on infrastructure; own the clinical systems layer they don't touch
Product Operations & Launch
Own bug intake and prioritization from Market Operations — standardize how Engineering receives, scopes, and resolves issues and communicates status back to the field
Build structured launch toolkits and training materials so clinic teams are prepared for new feature rollouts on day one
Coordinate end-to-end launches across Product, Engineering, and Operations
Identify where AI and automation can reduce manual administrative burden in product operations workflows
Standards & Knowledge Management
Build and maintain the clinical systems SOP library so new market setup is repeatable — documented well enough that a new hire can execute without you in the room
Develop onboarding materials for clinic managers and clinical staff on EHR workflows and tooling
Drive feature parity efforts so patients and clinicians experience a consistent standard of care across markets
Data & Reporting
Build and maintain dashboards tracking feature adoption, issue resolution, and rollout health across clinics
Develop quarterly reporting for Product, leadership, and health system partners on platform performance
Ensure data infrastructure is in place to measure the impact of every feature rollout

3+ years with product operations, technical program management, or PM-adjacent work — ideally at a growth-stage digital health or services company
Strong problem-solving instincts and genuine curiosity — you like figuring out how things work and making them work better
Ease with ambiguity and a bias toward action; this role requires you to create the playbook, not execute someone else's
Demonstrated ability to navigate complex stakeholder environments and drive aggressive timelines — ideally with client-facing or health system-facing experience
Ability to speak ‘multiple languages’ – comfort going deep on technical details while communicating clearly to non-technical audiences; you can write a bug ticket, an SOP, and a launch plan that people actually follow; hands-on EHR configuration and integration experience strongly preferred
Analytical enough to build a dashboard and identify a pattern, even if you're not a SQL expert
What Success Looks Like
In your first 90 days, you've audited our current Athena configuration, identified gaps, and have a remediation plan. You understand the bug triage process well enough to have improved it. You've met your counterparts at every health system partner and know what's coming for the next Epic integration.
At six months, new market launches have a repeatable systems and product checklist. Clinic teams know what to expect before a feature goes live. Bug resolution time is measurably faster and the field is no longer sending issues into a black hole.
At one year, the SOP library is comprehensive, clinical systems configuration is stable and documented, and you've successfully navigated at least one new health system EHR environment. The product team has a reliable partner and the ops team isn't dependent on any single person for systems knowledge.

We are looking for a Principal Product Manager to drive product strategy and product management across the Core Banking domain and to own the most complex, cross-functional core related initiatives. This is a senior individual-contributor role: you set direction, connect product strategy to the platform's technical strategy, and deliver measurable outcomes in partnership with engineering.
You will operate with a high degree of autonomy, sponsoring pre-consensus bets with a written thesis, setting operating rhythms for the Core PM group, and influencing VP/SVP stakeholders through documented trade-offs. You will be an authority on how a core banking system actually works — down to posting logic — and pair that with strong traditional product-management judgment across pricing, risk, product performance, compliance, legal, GTM, and partnerships.

With your PM colleagues, own and drive product strategy and roadmap across multiple Core domains (e.g., deposits, postings/ledger, product factory, transactions) and the end-to-end core product.
The most complex cross-company initiatives — including core conversion enablement and US market-expansion capabilities.
Connecting product strategy to org-level technical strategy; anchoring build vs. buy vs. partner.
Product GTM with measurable outcomes and documented reviews, in partnership with Marketing, Sales, Ops, and client teams.
Operating models and planning frameworks for the Core PM group; standards and playbooks other PMs build on.
Regulatory posture and responsible-AI principles embedded into the Core product.
Product Strategy & Roadmapping
With your PM colleagues define and own multi-domain product strategy and the multi-quarter roadmap for Core Banking.
Translate business, regulatory, and client needs into clear product outcomes; frame problems others haven't yet articulated.
Conduct appropriate research and synthesize findings.
Make informed trade-offs across speed, quality, scalability, and regulatory requirements.
Delivery & Execution
Partner with Engineering Managers on prioritization, sequencing, planning, and dependency management across teams and squads.
Set operating rhythms and planning frameworks; remove cross-team hurdles and drive quality and velocity improvements.
Maintain a coherent, prioritized product direction as priorities shift.
Stakeholder & Client Collaboration
Act as the senior product interface for business, operations, compliance, risk, legal, and technology stakeholders.
Influence VP/SVP decisions through documented prioritization and signed trade-offs (timeline, risk, cost).
Represent the Core product with external banking clients and internal SoFi Bank partners.
Technical & Platform Leadership
Apply posting-logic-level understanding of core banking (accounts, double-entry ledger, postings, interest, product catalog, batch vs. real-time).
Challenge business architectural assumptions at the system and cross-org level; prevent unnecessary complexity and maintenance burden.
Ensure the Core product meets the requirements of US-chartered banking entities.
What you’ll need
Bachelor's degree in computer science or relevant field
Deep, hands-on understanding of the inner workings of a core banking system — ideally at the posting-logic / double-entry ledger level.
A track record of building or product-managing a core banking product itself (a platform/vendor perspective) — as opposed to running core conversion or transformation programs inside a bank.
Strong traditional product-management background across several of: pricing, risk, compliance, product performance, legal, communication, partnering, and go-to-market.
A very good understanding of the US banking market and its regulatory environment.
10+ years of professional experience, with significant time in Product Management for complex, regulated technology platforms.
Demonstrated ability to drive strategy across multiple product areas and lead the most complex cross-functional initiatives with a high degree of autonomy.
Excellent written and verbal communication in English; able to shape company-level product communication and executive-ready written theses.

LatAm core banking exposure and/or Spanish-language proficiency.
Experience with modern, API-first, cloud-native core platforms and microservices architectures.
Familiarity with the competitive landscape (e.g., Thought Machine, 10x, Mambu, Finxact, FIS, Fiserv, Jack Henry, Temenos).
Experience selling or supporting a core platform for external financial-institution clients as well as an in-house bank.

Truecaller's ads business reaches over 400 million users and is one of the largest in-app advertising platforms in its markets.

We are building a modern, server-driven programmatic stack that we own end to end, and this role owns the platform at the heart of it: the intelligence layer that powers demand-supply matching across all our demand channels.

Every ad opportunity flows through this platform, and it decides how that opportunity is valued, priced, auctioned, and allocated to maximize revenue while protecting user experience.
This is a senior, high-ownership role at the center of a multi-year platform build, working closely with engineering, data science, and the supply and demand product teams.

Own the platform strategy and roadmap: the decisioning, auction, and pricing systems that sit between our supply and our demand partners.
Build auction intelligence: bid landscape analysis, pricing and floor strategies, auction design, and demand orchestration that decides which demand sources to invoke for each opportunity.
Drive yield: deliver measurable improvements in eCPM, fill, win rate, and incremental revenue; identify revenue leakage and close it through platform enhancements.
Optimize for scale: drive initiatives around platform performance, reliability, and latency as traffic volumes and demand partners grow.
Shape the long-term architecture: capabilities like traffic shaping, audience-based packaging, and curated marketplaces that turn the platform into a durable competitive advantage.
Run a rigorous operating cadence: define platform KPIs and operational health metrics, design controlled experiments, and iterate based on measured impact.

6+ years in product management, with 3+ years in ad tech, programmatic advertising, or publisher monetization platforms. Hands-on experience driving revenue growth through programmatic is essential.
Programmatic depth: Strong understanding of the ecosystem, including unified auctions, header bidding, open bidding, mediation models, oRTB, and auction dynamics. Working knowledge of platforms such as Google Ad Manager, PubMatic, or ironSource.
Monetization fluency: comfort with the full KPI stack (eCPM, fill rate, match rate, win rate, bid density, viewability, ARPU) and a track record of using it to find and capture yield.
Platform product skills: proven experience building large-scale platform products with engineering-heavy teams, and the ability to translate complex business problems into scalable platform capabilities. Good understanding of distributed systems, APIs, and latency-sensitive architecture.
Data-driven rigor: strong analytical skills, comfort with large datasets, and fluency in experimentation, A/B testing, and controlled rollouts.
Stakeholder influence: ability to align engineering, data science, ad operations, and sales around a common platform strategy using data and business insight.

You will be fully responsible for keeping every workstream moving to standard - setting priorities with stakeholders, translating them into clear technical tasks, driving delivery across product, engineering, design, data, and marketing, and taking direct ownership of projects that have no dedicated owner.
This is a high-accountability role suited for someone who treats "almost done" as not done. We hold a high bar: clear tickets, honest timelines, and work shipped to standard. You will inspect the work, keep the team moving when pace or quality slips, and close gaps yourself when a project falls between roles.

Execution Ownership & Process
Set priorities together with stakeholders and maintain a single, agreed backlog
Own the delivery pipeline end to end, from prioritized backlog to verified release
Define and enforce processes, definitions of done, and quality standards across all workstreams
Drive sprint planning, task tracking, and follow-through so nothing stalls silently
Identify process bottlenecks and fix them with structure, not workarounds
Task Definition & Technical Clarity
Translate product and business priorities into precise, developer-ready technical tasks
Write specs with clear acceptance criteria, edge cases, and measurable outcomes
Partner with engineering to scope, estimate, and sequence work realistically
Use AI tools daily to accelerate spec writing, analysis, and QA - and spread what works across the team
Verify delivered work against spec before it ships — and reject what falls short
Standards & Team Accountability
Hold every contributor to explicit quality and deadline expectations
Push pace and raise the bar when execution drifts, directly and constructively
Run reviews and retros that convert misses into changed processes
Institutionalize best practices so quality does not depend on individual heroics
Cross-functional & Unowned Projects
Take direct ownership of initiatives that lack a dedicated owner and drive them to completion
Coordinate across product, engineering, design, data, and marketing to unblock dependencies
Collaborate with the Managing Director to align execution priorities with business goals
Keep stakeholders informed with concise, honest status reporting

Must-Have Experience
3+ years as a Project Owner, Product Manager, or Delivery/Project Lead on a live software product
Proven track record writing technical tasks and specs that engineers execute without back-and-forth
Experience running agile delivery processes (backlog management, sprints, releases) end to end
Demonstrated ability to build processes, checklists, and quality standards - not just follow them
Experience holding cross-functional contributors accountable for deadlines and quality
Working technical fluency: able to discuss implementation trade-offs with engineers credibly
Advanced, daily use of AI tools (LLMs, agents, AI-assisted workflows) to accelerate specs, analysis, and delivery - with command of standard task-management tooling (Jira, Linear, Notion, or equivalent)
Leadership Attributes
Highly structured operator - you build systems that make quality repeatable
Comfortable giving direct, specific feedback and enforcing standards without drama
Bias to ownership: picks up unclaimed problems instead of waiting for assignment
Detail-obsessed about the work itself - reads the ticket, tests the feature, checks the numbers
Clear, direct communicator who operates effectively in a remote environment
Location

Docker has been one of the most loved brands in developer tooling, trusted by more than 20 million monthly users and over 20 billion container image pulls. From solo founders to the world's largest companies, developers rely on Docker to build, share, and run their applications across our suite of products including Docker Desktop, Docker Hub, and Docker Scout.
We are a globally distributed, remote-first team building the tools that define how software gets built and delivered. As AI agents redefine software development, Docker is at the center of that shift, providing the sandboxed environments, verified images, and secure infrastructure that make autonomous workflows trustworthy by default.
AI agents are changing how everyone works — not just developers writing code, but entire organizations building, deploying, and operating software. Agents are becoming teammates: they write code, run tests, manage infrastructure, analyze data, and automate workflows across every function.

Docker is building a new platform from scratch to make this real — secure execution environments, agent-to-tool connectivity, governance controls, and the infrastructure that lets agents and humans collaborate safely at enterprise scale.
This is a 0-to-1 role. You will define the product strategy and own the roadmap for a new platform that sits at the intersection of AI, containers, and developer experience. You will work with a small, high-velocity team spanning engineering, design, and go-to-market to figure out what to build, ship it, learn from it, and iterate. The early signal is already in market — Docker Sandboxes is one of the fastest-growing new products in Docker’s history — and the opportunity ahead is much larger.
We are looking for someone who builds, not just plans. You should be comfortable prototyping, getting your hands dirty with early product iterations, and improvising when things don’t go as expected. The right candidate has shipped developer tools or infrastructure products, understands how the agentic AI ecosystem is evolving, and thrives in the ambiguity of building something genuinely new.

Own the product strategy. Define the vision, roadmap, and success metrics for Docker’s AI & Agent Platform. Make hard tradeoff decisions about what to build, what to defer, and what to cut.
Build from zero. This is a new platform. You will define the product from the ground up — writing the first specs, prototyping with engineering, validating with customers, and iterating rapidly based on what you learn.
Drive from conception through delivery. Write requirements, work with engineering to scope and prioritize, ship iteratively, and measure outcomes. You don’t hand off specs and wait — you are in the details.
Define how pieces of the agentic ecosystem fit together. Agents need secure execution, tool connectivity, model access, governance, and observability. You will define how these capabilities compose into a coherent platform — and where Docker’s boundaries are.
Think beyond developers. Agents are becoming essential for everyone who builds, deploys, and operates software. You will ensure the platform serves the full range of people who need agents to succeed — from individual developers to platform teams to enterprise operators.
Define the developer experience. Work with design and engineering to ensure that our AI products are intuitive, powerful, and meet people where they are — whether in the CLI, IDE, or CI pipeline.
Collaborate across Docker. You will work cross-functionally to ensure coherent product experiences and go-to-market alignment.
Influence technical direction. Partner with engineering leadership on architecture decisions. You don’t need to write the code, but you need to understand the technical tradeoffs and have informed opinions about them.
Represent the customer. Engage directly with developers, enterprises, and partners. Bring their voice into every product decision.
Overcome blockers. When something is in the way — a missing integration, an unclear market signal, a technical constraint — you figure out a path forward. You don’t wait for someone else to solve the problem.

Experience . 10+ years of product management experience, with at least 5 years on developer tools, infrastructure, or platform products.
Deep technical fluency. You can read an architecture diagram, understand container and VM runtimes, and have a working knowledge of how AI agents, LLMs, and protocol-level tool connectivity work. You don’t need to be a hypervisor engineer, but you need to hold your own with one.
Proven ability to ship 0-to-1 products. You have taken a product from idea through launch in a fast-moving environment. You know how to operate when there is no playbook.
Builder mentality. You prototype, you sketch architectures, you test early ideas with customers before the spec is done. You are a doer, not just a thinker.
Strong product sense and UX instincts. You care about the developer experience at a deep level — from API design to CLI ergonomics to error messages.
Strategic thinking with execution follow-through. You can set a multi-year vision and also write the spec for what ships next sprint.
Comfort with ambiguity. This space is new and moving fast. You thrive when the answer isn’t obvious and you have to go find it.
Excellent communication. You can write a crisp product brief, present to executives, and debate technical tradeoffs with engineers — all in the same day.
Experience growing and monetizing products at scale. You have been part of taking a product from early adoption to meaningful revenue, and you understand the pricing, packaging, and go-to-market decisions that make that happen.

Experience building products in the containers, cloud-native, or DevOps space
Experience with AI/ML developer tooling or the agentic AI ecosystem
Contributions to open source projects
Experience building and scaling a business from zero to significant ARR
What You’ll Work With
We are building a new platform for agentic development. Docker Sandboxes — isolated execution environments for AI coding agents — is one of the first products in this platform and one of the fastest-growing new products in Docker’s history. But this is just the beginning. The platform will grow to span multiple product areas as we define how agents and people work together at scale.

Position Summary: We're hiring a Senior Product Manager to drive strategy and execution for the technology behind Sales and Service at Hornblower. While you own the platforms the Sales, Service, and Contact Center teams sell and serve on, those teams own their operations and their people.

This role is the IT-side product owner for the Sales & Service organizations, where you will serve as a peer to your Sales-org and Marketing-org counterparts. In this role you will need to land outcomes through partnership while leading through influence.

On the Sales side you own the technology for every non-web channel — contact center sales, group and event sales, partners and third parties, and OTA bookings. On the Service side you own service technology for every channel, web and OTA included, from pre-booking inquiry through post-booking support.

Web sales itself sits with the Digital team — because the guest journey crosses that line constantly, you'll partner closely with Digital wherever their surface and yours meet.The problems aren't fully framed yet, the stakeholder map is wide (Sales, Contact Center, Marketing, Digital, plus vendors like Anchor and Salesforce and several consultancies), and the right answer generally isn't sitting in anyone's backlog.

You'll shape it as the first dedicated product owner for this scope, in close partnership with the Head of Product. Duties and Responsibilities:
Drive the enterprise roadmap for Sales and Service technology, framing the problems worth solving and sequencing the bets across channels, vendors, and internal teams.
Shape the technology strategy and the measurement approach behind it — define what good looks like for non-web sales (contact center, group/event, partners, OTA) and for cross-channel service, and the metrics we'll hold ourselves to.
Navigate the internal-and-vendor stakeholder map and lead without authority to a single coherent plan people can commit to.
Partner closely with the Digital team at the web/non-web seam — Digital owns the web sales surface, you own everything else in sales and all of service, and the guest journey crosses that boundary constantly. Make the seam invisible to the guest.
Influence senior partners across IT and the business to make the contested tradeoffs — build vs. buy, vendor vs. internal, sales-channel-specific vs. shared service capability — and own the rationale behind those calls.
Partner with engineering and vendor teams on architecture tradeoffs across a multi-platform ecosystem; bring a clear technical point of view to decisions about Anchor, Salesforce, and the integrations between them.
Drive execution against the roadmap across multi-quarter horizons, sequencing near-term wins in contact center, group/partner sales, OTA, and cross-channel service so they compound into the longer-arc strategy.
What success looks like (first 6–12 months)
You've published an enterprise roadmap for Sales and Service technology that the business, IT leadership, the Digital team, and key vendors are aligned to — and that holds up when priorities shift.
You've reframed at least one ambiguous problem in the scope (e.g., what "service" actually means across web, OTA, contact center, and partner bookings) and shipped a strategy others now plan against.
You've moved a meaningful metric in either non-web sales (including OTA) or cross-channel service, and can attribute the impact. You've built a working rhythm with the Digital team where web/non-web boundary calls — what belongs to Digital, what belongs to you, what's shared — get made cleanly and quickly, not relitigated.
Senior stakeholders across Sales, Contact Center, Marketing, and Digital bring you the hard tradeoffs instead of routing around the roadmap.

Multiple prior cycles of driving strategy and execution for an ambiguous, multi-stakeholder domain — you've done this more than once, not just adjacent to it.
A demonstrated ability to find and frame the right problems when the mandate is fuzzy and the stakeholder map is fragmented.
Experience building enterprise or cross-channel roadmaps that align internal business partners and external vendors to a shared plan.
A track record of landing cross-functional decisions with senior stakeholders you don't report to — functions that don't report into you or each other now move together because of how you ran the call.
A clear point of view on how to measure success for sales and service outcomes, and the data fluency to define metrics rather than just consume dashboards.
Able to engage engineering and vendor teams on architecture tradeoffs — integration approaches, platform choices, build-vs-buy — and explain the reasoning behind your position.

Background in maritime, hospitality, travel, or experiences — particularly on the sales or service side.
Hands-on experience with Salesforce as a product surface.
Familiarity with ticketing platforms, especially Anchor or Ventrata.
Comfort in the Atlassian Suite (JIRA, Confluence) as your working environment.
Practical use of AI tools (Claude, Codex, or similar) in your PM workflow — research, synthesis, spec drafting, prototyping.

We are looking for a Lead Product Manager to own the future of the Lattice MCP (Model Context Protocol) server and the integrations that power Lattice AI.

This is the connective layer that lets customers use Lattice performance data inside the AI tools they already work in (Claude, ChatGPT, Glean, Microsoft Copilot, and Slack), and that brings third-party productivity data (e.g., Jira, GitHub, Linear, Zoom, Asana) into Lattice.

As AI becomes the center of gravity for how companies work, this surface is how Lattice stays connected, interoperable, and indispensable. You’ll join a fully staffed engineering team ready to execute, and together you’ll make ecosystem interoperability a reason customers choose and stay with Lattice.
If you enjoy solving complex problems, shaping platform strategy, and working with great internal and external partners, you’ll love the impact you can have here. As a Lead Product Manager for MCP & AI Ecosystem, you will:
Own the MCP and AI ecosystem strategy. Not only decide what features and integrations to pursue, but what MCP and AI mean to Lattice and our customers. Become a thought leader on how AI should shape HR for the better.
Ship integrations that create leverage. Deliver new MCP tools, resources, and third-party connectors that expand what admins, managers, and executives can do with Lattice data in the flow of work.
Build durable foundations, like authentication, agentic execution frameworks, and evals that make future integrations faster, more scalable, and easier to adopt and maintain.
Be a technical thought partner to Engineering. Help shape technical direction on MCP tool design and third party integration infrastructure, translating complex constraints into clear product decisions.
Drive go-to-market with partners. Partner with Partnerships, Product Marketing, to launch integrations that deliver measurable customer and ecosystem impact.
Own outcomes. Influence and own key results across integration and MCP adoption, reliability, activation, and ecosystem growth.
What You Will Bring to the Table
We’re looking for a seasoned product manager with the technical depth and strategic instincts to shape Lattice’s next generation of integrations and APIs. You’ll be a great fit if you have a combination of:
7+ years of product management experience, with meaningful ownership of integrations, platform, or ecosystem surfaces (built end-to-end, not just configured).
Direct experience building technical integrations in a multi-party ecosystem — for example ad technology / marketing technology, marketplaces, developer platforms, payments, data connectivity, or similar — where partnership strategy shaped what you built.
Strong technical fluency: comfortable with third-party integration patterns, data sync and field mapping, webhooks, and auth/OAuth; you can hold a credible architecture conversation with engineers and partner CTOs.
A track record of shipping scalable, reliable integrations in partnership with engineering, and of standing up partner or marketplace launches with go-to-market teams.
Evidence of turning a platform or ecosystem into a competitive advantage — a reason customers chose your product, not just a checkbox.
Clear, confident communication that brings internal teams and external partners into alignment.
A bias for action and the ability to create structure in an ambiguous, fast-moving space.

Exposure to AI ecosystems, MCP, AI agents, or LLM tooling (helpful, not required).
Experience in multi-product B2B SaaS, or with HR/people-data or other sensitive-data workflows.
If you have strong experience with integrations, APIs, or platform products, even if you don’t meet every preferred qualification, we encourage you to apply. We’re looking for strong product thinkers with deep technical fluency, not perfect resumes.

Webflow is the agentic web marketing platform for modern marketing teams, helping organizations build, manage, and optimize high-performing web experiences that drive predictable growth and strengthen brand trust. Building at Webflow will need grit, because we move fast, without ever sacrificing craft or quality.
We're looking for an experienced Product Manager to own how people extend Webflow with code, whether they're developers writing it themselves or the AI agents increasingly writing it alongside them. Our Code team builds the surfaces that bring code-based primitives into Webflow and keep them in sync with the rest of the platform.
This is where Webflow's visual canvas meets real code. It's one of the hardest and most interesting seams in the product, connecting a visual way of building to the code underneath it so that neither one holds the other back. You'll own that seam, deciding how far the two worlds reach into each other and making the connection feel native to developers and agents.

Location: Remote-first (Argentina)
Full-time
Permanent, full-time employee (this is not a contractor position)

Application deadline: applications accepted on an ongoing basis until position is closed and filled
This posting is for a new position
Reporting to the Director of Product Management, Develop
As a Senior Product Manager, Code, you’ll …
Build for developers and AI agents alike. You'll design surfaces that serve the developers who have always worked in code and the AI agents that increasingly write it, treating both as first-class users.
Own the roadmap and delivery across the Code surfaces. You'll lead the products that let developers and agents extend Webflow with code, starting with code components, in close partnership with Engineering, Design, and Data.
Define what "good" means for extensibility. You'll set the quality bar for developer-grade extensibility, including the hard problem of keeping a visual product and real code faithful to each other as each side changes.
Make it all work as one. Several of these surfaces grew up separately. Sequence the work so the pieces reinforce each other and build shared primitives once, rather than solving the same problem twice.
Contribute heavily to strategy, then ship it. You'll help shape where the area goes and turn that into a roadmap you deliver against, working as a partner rather than waiting to be handed direction.
Get into the code. This is a hands-on role. You'll prototype, read and reason about code, and stay close enough to the implementation to make sharp technical calls.
Place durable bets in a shifting landscape. Developer tooling and AI-assisted coding are moving fast, and you'll make choices that hold up as the tools and the ecosystem evolve.

BA/BS degree or equivalent experience
Business-level fluency to read, write and speak in English

s.h: You’ll thrive as a a Senior Product Manager, Code, if you
s.t:
Have 5+ years of product management experience, with real depth in developer or platform products. Experience with APIs, extensibility, or developer tooling.
Are genuinely technical. You read and reason about code, hold a point of view on API and abstraction design, and are comfortable working in a codebase rather than just adjacent to one.
Relate to your users and hold more than one perspective at once. You have real empathy for the people you build for and can see a problem through several sets of eyes, balancing needs that pull in different directions without losing sight of any of them.
Enjoy the full craft of building software. You're curious about every part of how products get made and like getting into the details wherever the work needs you, whether that's leading a user interview, prototyping an idea, writing a query to pin down a metric, or writing a sharp brief.
Work as a peer and a thought partner. You shape direction alongside your manager and then run with it independently, at home in a player-coach partnership rather than a top-down chain of command.
Stay curious, building fluency in emerging AI and developer tooling to speed up both your own work and your team's.
Genuinely enjoy helping people build. You like being close to the developers and teammates you serve, and helping someone ship something they couldn't before is the part of the job that keeps it fun.

Win together. We play to win, and we win as one team. Success at Webflow isn't a solo act.

You sit between Sales and Engineering and translate in both directions. Towards Sales: which use cases we can sell today, which we cannot, and what a demo is allowed to claim. The product roadmap and the reasoning behind it: what we build next, in which order, and what we decline.
The boundary between standard product, configuration, and manual work for one customer.
Requirements that engineering can build from: scope, acceptance criteria, and a clear statement of what is out.
What we can credibly promise a customer, including where the product's limits currently are.
Proofs of Value that you run yourself, and responsibility for individual accounts.
Prototypes you build to test features with customers before we commit engineering time.
How product works here: discovery, prioritisation, and the standards between product and engineering.
Your number: how much of what is project work today is standard product a year from now, and the time from a recognised customer problem to a usable capability.

🌎 What we do
We build software to enable sustainable agriculture supply chains.
~31% of global GHG emissions originate from food-related activities. For the first time in history, climate performance has become an overall business performance indicator.

Enterprises are mandated by regulatory bodies to disclose their climate performance, which leads to increasing pressure from investors, competitors, retailers, and consumers to prevent and reduce their CO2e emissions. Over the next 10 years, companies have set ambitious reduction targets that need to be met.

Enterprise software and new business processes can help - to make processes in the day-to-day more efficient, connect farmers better to their partners and thus, enable action in supply chains.
We raised >€10m in funding in the first 2 years of our existence, we launched our enterprise product, signed and onboarded some of the largest F&B players in Europe, and put together what we believe is the best-suited early stage tech team in Europe.
Today Root is the #1 primary data collection platform for dairy in DACH. We are AI-enabled at the core and driving the AI transformation across the food and agri world. The next chapter is bigger.
🔭 What you will work on

Build an innovative operating system for the dairy industry from 0 to 1, at the intersection of farmers and dairies. Dairy is Root's home market. We know it inside out - the players, the workflows, the technology gaps, the people. We see a category-defining opportunity to build a new product line that sits between farmers and dairy processors, and that has the potential to become the connecting piece of our portfolio.
This is a genuinely greenfield role. You will not inherit a backlog. You will define what we build, why, and for whom - then prove it works with a handful of pilot customers before we scale.

s.h: What your job will look like
s.t:
Run deep discovery. Spend weeks with farmers, farm technicians, milk procurement teams, and dairy executives on-site. Understand their jobs, KPIs, and frustrations from the inside.
Define new workflows together with our customers. Shape how dairy companies will work in the future. This product line is about setting a new standard, not digitising what already exists - while AI will be at the core of it.
Build hacky prototypes and run pilots. Show, do not tell. Get something tangible in front of 2-3 design partners within weeks.
Assess desirability, feasibility, and viability before we commit serious engineering investment.
Define the v1 spec with engineering and design once we have conviction. Set the team up for delivery.
Onboard the first paying customers and iterate fast. Own the loop.
Decide what we will NOT build. Scope discipline is critical with limited engineering capacity and a customer base that operates on a fixed annual cycle.
You will work side by side with the Head of Product to make the bet, and own the product line end-to-end as it grows. Engineering and design support will scale with traction.

s.h: What success looks like at 6 months
s.t:
A first end-to-end prototype tested with real customers
3 signed Letters of Intent from new customers
A concrete, evidence-backed set of build hypotheses for v1
🦾 How we support you
You will report directly to our Head of Product.

About Wizard Wizard is the top-performing AI Shopping Agent, delivering the best products from across the web with unmatched accuracy, quality, and trust. We're redefining how people shop by combining AI reasoning with real-time commerce.

Instead of searching through dozens of websites, consumers simply tell Wizard what they're looking for, and our AI agent finds, compares, and recommends the best products from across the internet.

As we continue scaling, we're building the merchant platform that powers this experience—connecting retailers, brands, product catalogs, pricing, availability, offers, checkout, and merchant insights into a seamless ecosystem.

About the Role We're looking for a Product Manager, Merchant Experience to own the merchant side of Wizard 's AI shopping ecosystem.

You'll define the strategy and roadmap for the products that enable merchants to successfully sell through Wizard from merchant onboarding and integrations to catalog quality, pricing, promotions, monetization, reporting, and merchant insights.

You'll own the merchant-facing experience, including the long-term vision for the merchant dashboard, analytics, and reporting capabilities. You'll help answer a critical question for Wizard : What products, tools, and insights will merchants log into and rely on.

Working closely with Merchant Partnerships, Engineering, AI, Data, Merchant Operations, and Partner Success, you'll build scalable products that help merchants maximize visibility, conversion, and revenue while ensuring consumers receive the best shopping experience. This role sits at the intersection of commerce, product, and AI.

You'll balance merchant needs with consumer experience while shaping how retailers and brands participate in the next generation of AI-powered shopping. What You'll Do
Own the vision, strategy, and roadmap for Wizard 's merchant platform and merchant-facing product experiences.
Build products that help merchants onboard quickly, manage catalogs, optimize product visibility, understand performance, and grow sales through Wizard .
Define and evolve the merchant dashboard, reporting experience, and merchant insights roadmap, delivering meaningful visibility into performance, catalog health, attribution, conversion, and business outcomes.
Define experiences around merchant onboarding, catalog management, pricing, promotions, inventory, offers, checkout, APIs, and merchant reporting.
Partner closely with Merchant Partnerships to translate retailer feedback and strategic partner needs into scalable product capabilities.
Work with Engineering to build APIs, merchant integrations, feeds, and platform capabilities that make it easy for retailers and brands to integrate with Wizard .
Collaborate with AI and Search teams to improve how merchant data is surfaced, ranked, and personalized throughout the shopping journey.
Partner with Data to define the metrics, dashboards, and reporting capabilities that power merchant decision-making today while laying the foundation for future paid merchant intelligence products.
Drive initiatives that improve merchant adoption, catalog quality, product coverage, conversion, engagement, and monetization.
Balance merchant requests with long-term platform investments that scale across thousands of merchants.
Establish KPIs around merchant growth, dashboard engagement, catalog quality, product coverage, conversion, merchant retention, and revenue.
Meet regularly with strategic merchants to validate product direction and identify new opportunities.

5–8+ years of Product Management experience building commerce, marketplace, retail technology, ecommerce, payments, or merchant products.
Experience owning merchant-facing or B2B products that drive adoption, engagement, monetization, or merchant growth.
Strong understanding of ecommerce ecosystems, product catalogs, pricing, promotions, inventory, checkout, APIs, merchant integrations, and reporting platforms.
Strong understanding of the metrics retailers and brands care about, including GMV, traffic, conversion, AOV, product visibility, attribution, customer intent, promotional performance, catalog health, and reporting quality.
Experience partnering with Business Development, Merchant Partnerships, or Sales teams to launch external-facing products.
Experience building dashboards, analytics products, reporting experiences, or data-driven customer products is highly preferred.
Strong product intuition with the ability to balance merchant needs, consumer experience, and business objectives.
Experience working cross-functionally with Engineering, Design, AI, Data, Partnerships, and GTM teams.
Analytical mindset with experience using data to drive product decisions and prioritization.
Comfortable operating in a fast-paced startup environment with significant ambiguity.
You'll Thrive Here If You...
Enjoy building products that help merchants grow their business.
Think deeply about marketplace dynamics and balancing the needs of both merchants and consumers.
Can translate complex commerce workflows into intuitive product experiences.
Are excited by building dashboards, reporting, and insights that merchants genuinely rely on.
Love building products from zero to one in an early-stage startup.
Thrive collaborating across engineering, partnerships, commercial, and data teams.

Equity in the form of stock options

401(k)

At the N2 Company, our vision is " to be the most respected franchise in the nation, to share stories that build community, and to provide meaningful work for our team". About Us The N2 Company is America’s leading publisher of community magazines.

We’re proud of our award-winning media brands – they reach millions of readers in nearly every state and help great businesses connect with ideal clients – but we’re even more proud to provide supportive and fulfilling remote work opportunities for our people.

About The Role As our new Social Media Product Manager, you'll be leading the performance and evolution of two of our most important social media products.

You'll oversee the strategy and growth of Pub Pulse, our organic Facebook and Instagram program supporting hundreds of franchisee accounts, and our Lead Generation Program, which manages a growing portfolio of Facebook advertising campaigns.

Working closely with leadership, you'll shape the future of both programs by driving strategy, optimizing systems and reporting, and identifying opportunities to improve performance and scalability.

While dedicated strategists handle day-to-day execution, you’ll focus on the bigger picture by shaping strategy, improving processes, and creating scalable solutions that help both products thrive and deliver meaningful results for our franchise network. This is a fully remote position. Interviews will be conducted via phone and video calls.

The salary range is $70,000-$80,000 annually, with opportunities for growth and advancement. The Role in Action
Drive the strategy and performance of Pub Pulse and our Facebook Lead Generation Program, helping hundreds of franchisees grow through organic and paid social media.
Optimize Facebook advertising performance across a large portfolio of campaigns by maximizing results, improving lead quality, and driving measurable business impact.
Develop KPIs, reporting, and data-driven insights that guide decisions, improve product performance, and support long-term growth.
Lead testing initiatives and continuously improve workflows, automation, and processes to increase efficiency and scalability.
Partner with leadership to shape product strategy, prioritize enhancements, and drive the future direction of both programs.
Serve as the go-to expert for Facebook advertising, social media strategy, and product optimization across the organization.
The Ideal Candidate We’re looking for someone who will hit the ground running with:
5+ years of experience in social media advertising, paid media, digital marketing, product management, or a related field with a track record of driving results.
Proven experience managing high-volume Meta (Facebook/Instagram) advertising portfolios, including multiple campaigns, markets, audiences, and budgets.
Experience optimizing paid social campaigns with a focus on efficiency, lead quality, and return on investment, including small and mid-sized budgets.
Strong knowledge of Meta Ads Manager, Meta Business Suite, and social media management platforms such as Cloud Campaign or similar tools.
Experience using project management tools like Monday.com and building scalable workflows, processes, and operational improvements.
Strong analytical, communication, leadership, and problem-solving skills with the ability to turn strategy into successful execution.

As Product Manager, you will be responsible for building and improving the experience on Newsela .

You will work cross-functionally with marketing, design, success, and fellow product managers, including the Supplemental ELA product manager, to ensure that features meet the needs of teachers and students in the classroom. You will identify opportunities, track performance, and build features that drive the largest possible impact.

What You'll Be Doing:
Build features and tools that directly impact teachers and students.
Own the platform experience through collaboration: define what gets built, why, and in what order, in close partnership with the engineering team.
Work directly with design and internal content/ELA pedagogy experts throughout the product lifecycle, from discovery to launch, to validate that features solve real classroom challenges.
Partner closely with a fast-moving, AI-forward engineering team to deliver high-impact features.
Translate ambiguous problems into clear priorities and hold cross-functional partners accountable to scope and timelines.
Use data to determine what is working, what isn't, and where the greatest opportunity lies.

You have 3+ years of experience in a Product Management function scaling new or existing products.
Experience in EdTech, K-12 education, SaaS,or working with instructional products strongly preferred .
Experience working closely with design and subject-matter experts (content, pedagogy, or similar) to shape features, beyond simply handing off requirements.
Demonstrated comfort using AI tools as part of a daily product management workflow, with genuine enthusiasm for a team that builds with AI at its core.
Strong analytical skills, with the ability to dig into data directly rather than relying on others for answers.
All offers of employment are contingent upon the successful completion of a background check as part of our pre-employment process. Why you’ll love working at Newsela :

Health & Wellness: Comprehensive medical benefits with employer contribution to premiums and to HSA accounts. Additional benefits such as gym reimbursement, pet insurance, free access to the Calm app, Rocket Lawyer and more to help you stay healthy: mind, body, and soul.

Work From Home: We are a fully remote company. We provide a monthly tech stipend to support your WFH needs!

Supporting ALL Families: Inclusive benefits to support you and your family, including parental leave, fertility support, adoption, and more!

Financial Wellbeing: Invest in your future with our 401(k) plan, which includes a employer match to help you build long-term financial security.

Time Off: Flexible PTO, paid sick time off, company holidays plus winter break (Dec 24th - Jan 1st).

Professional Development: Newsela offers an annual learning and development allowance to employees to attend external training sessions, classes, workshops, conferences, and educational materials to foster professional growth within their current role and career aspirations at Newsela .

Make A Difference: No matter your role or department, the work you do each day helps share the future of education and improves the lives of students and teachers.
About Newsela : Newsela is a leading education technology company dedicated to meaningful classroom learning for every student. We deliver integrated, AI-powered solutions designed to unlock student engagement, empower teachers, and drive meaningful learning outcomes.

Our suite of products supports knowledge and skill development, writing practice, daily instruction, assessment, and data-informed decision-making across K–12 classrooms.

Grounded in learning science research, Newsela ’s solutions integrate content, assessment, and analytics to help educators track progress, understand student outcomes, and deliver high-impact instruction that supports every learner.
